title: FTSE Russell on Bringing Index Data Onchain | The Future Is On Spotlight Series
description:
In this edition of The Future Is On, Kirsten Mierzwa, Head of Digital Assets at FTSE Russell, explains why bringing index data onchain is critical for the next generation of financial markets.

As institutions explore tokenized mutual funds, ETFs, and other onchain financial products, access to trusted benchmark data becomes essential.

Through its work with Chainlink, FTSE Russell is enabling secure, interoperable distribution of its index data across blockchain networks, ensuring accuracy and reliable tracking for tokenized assets.

asr.full_text: I've met so many people that are like, I am here because my firm is behind, I need to figure this out. We've got to start getting our data on chain. Hi. I'm Kristin Mirzwa. I'm the head of digital assets for FTSE Russell. FTSE Russell is an index provider that covers every asset class- equities, fixed income, Fx, commodities, and digital assets. We always felt strongly convicted that digital assets was an asset class in and of itself and that it was here to stay. So for us it's the growth engine of what are already very established business lines for us. us we think of working with chain link as another distribution arm for us to get our data into the hands of our asset managers and clients who are structuring financial product it's a very important railway and the financial ecosystem we believe that we're going to be in a multi chain world and we need to see interoperability happening and so to do that we want to make it as easy as possible for people to access our data on-chain via Chainlink. Imagine a world in TradPhi. People often use PE ratios or some of these traditional fundamentals to value an equity in a new on-chain world we're going to be able to marry a P.E. ratio with some behavioral finance that happens very quickly so you'll see trading behaviors happen over the weekend, and then you can take these two data points and put them together and have insights that you can implement in a much faster way. And what does that mean for everyone? That could mean that your able to get into a position or trade faster. That could mean you're able to protect risk in a way that you were never able to do in a very, very fast, efficient manner. We're seeing a lot of our clients thinking about wrapping product as tokens. So the tokenization wave. First it was mutual funds, then ETFs and now everyone's talking about, I want to run a tokenized fund. And they'll use our index data as the barometer or the benchmark for these funds and why it's important that this data is on chain is we want to make sure when someone's running a product a tokenized fund that they're actually tracking the benchmark that they say they're tracking, in a verified institutional quality way so investors know, hey, I'm getting that real exposure to whatever their index objective is. They can make their decisions faster and more accurate if they've got a trusted data source for, hey, when you're doing a trade you wanna make sure, am I trading asset A for asset B, and what is the clearing price for that? And how do I make that happen? So I think it's very, very important that we move to a higher quality set of data that is available on-chain. And I think a very obvious one that we're all seeing happening today is the idea of being able to do intraday repo in the dataset that we have, or two datasets that I think are pretty interesting for that space are our WMR FX rates. They're the world's institutional FX rates and then stablecoin rates. And I think everyone thinks stablecoins just trade at one but they don't. They're close to one, one way or another, but there is a secondary market for the price of stablecoins in a repo world that's a very important data point. FTSE Russell has a long history of partnering with technology firms Or someone who has a specialty that we don't have. We're indexing experts. Chainlink is an oracle and an expert at moving data around various blockchains. So it was a perfect partnership for the two of us to come together and get our data out there. A year ago, I don't think institutions were that worried about what was going on with crypto assets as a native asset class but in terms of tokenization and being able to take traditional products and structuring them on chain in a DeFi way, trying to eliminate costs in the structure for their clients and make everything more efficient, is top of mind for everyone. At SmartCon today, I've met so many people that are like I am here because my firm is behind. I need to figure this out. We've got to start getting our data on chain. At FTSE Russell, governance is the first and foremost place where we start with everything. And so we've got that all figured out. And one of the things that we're I would say, Russell governance is the first and foremost place where we start with everything. And so, we've got that all figured out. And one of the things that we're thinking about when we put our data on-chain to drive a smart contract is that it's immutable. What happens if the data source we use has a restatement? How can we push restatement through? And we will figure all these things out because there will be a way to do that. The technology and the creativity is there where you can say, okay we want to make sure the end client ends up with the highest quality data standard. We don't know exactly what blockchain everyone is going to start saying, hey corporate actions all sit on blockchain A or pricing data all sits on blockchain B so interoperability between the different environments because different block chains are built for different use cases but we all work together in an ecosystem so we want to make sure that the datasets can move between different environments or different block chains and we don't lose any kind of data quality when we do that. I think it will be the intersection of both TradFi and DeFi. DeFi is doing some things that we could all learn on the TradFi side, and of course there's lessons learned from all the years everyone's worked on the TradFi side that they can bring over to DeFi and maybe the two worlds together. And indices will end up being 24-7—truly 24-7— so that you can trade a market on the weekend. But what we need to do is have those underlying constituents trading 24-7 first. And then we're going get to that day where it's just everything is going all the time and you can manage risk in a much more efficient way. Chainlink has really stepped up and said hey there's a need for us to provide this platform to the traditional players and they've done a really good job educating traditional houses like the London Stock Exchange Group. About, hey, this this how we are going to take your data. This is how we're going to make sure it's secure and correct and verified. And then push it out on chain.

The visible studio interview and branded closing frame are consistent with the stated spotlight format.
